title: TRACE: Trajectory Correction from Cross-layer Evidence for Hallucination Reduction
abstract: arXiv:2605.18163v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Hallucination correction is not a one-direction problem. We show that intermediate layers are neither uniformly more truthful than final layers nor uniformly less trustworthy. Yet hallucination reduction is usually instantiated through one fixed intervention form: contrast one layer against another, steer along a truthfulness direction, or defer to external evidence. This framing is structurally incomplete. Cross-layer factual evidence does not evolve uniformly: in some failures truthful support is present internally and later suppressed, whereas in others candidate competition remains genuinely multi-directional across depth, so no single signed scalar family is generally sufficient. translated_title: TRACE：基于跨层证据的轨迹校正以减少幻觉
translated_abstract: 幻觉校正不是一个单向问题。我们表明，中间层既不总是比最终层更真实，也不总是更不可信。然而，幻觉减少通常通过一种固定的干预形式来实现：将某一层与另一层对比、沿着真实性方向进行引导，或者依赖外部证据。这种框架在结构上是不完整的。跨层事实证据的演化并不均匀：在某些失败情况中，真实支持存在于内部但随后被抑制；而在另一些情况中，候选答案之间的竞争在整个深度上仍然是真正的多向性的，因此任何单一的带符号标量族都无法普遍解决问题。我们提出了TRACE（基于跨层证据的轨迹校正以减少幻觉），这是一种确定性的、无需训练的算法，它通过推导出校正层以及适当的校正方式，在推理时校正幻觉。
tldr: 本文提出TRACE，一种无需训练的推理时幻觉校正算法，通过利用跨层事实证据的不均匀演化特性，动态确定校正层和相应的校正方式来减少大语言模型幻觉。
en_tdlr: TRACE is a deterministic, training-free algorithm that corrects hallucinations at inference time by leveraging the non-uniform evolution of cross-layer factual evidence to dynamically derive both the corrective layer and the appropriate correction strategy.
